clue.text: A chirpy host excited fund-raising outlet

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and agitated, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful landlord gets worked up about a shop raising money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges the eleven letters of A CHIRPY HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity shop sells donated goods to raise money for a good cause: a retail outlet for fund-raising.

clue.text: Be shifty in countryside row

definitions.meaning: to avoid giving a straight answer, to equivocate
a line of bushes bordering a field

explanation.surface: Someone behaves evasively during a rural quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to dodge commitment; a hedge is a row of shrubs dividing fields in the country.

clue.text: Free film for distribution?

definitions.meaning: a movie put out to cinemas

explanation.surface: Asks whether a free film is meant to be handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to set free; a release is also a new film or record issued to the public.

clue.text: Article is encapsulating second academic work

indicators.note: encapsulating means holding inside like a capsule, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing contains a second academic paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article is' reads as a phrase, but 'Article' and 'is' are separate pieces that together wrap round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation written for a degree is an extended piece of academic work.

clue.text: Waste in much of piazza bordering messy den

indicators.note: bordering means surrounding on the edges, so one piece goes around the other
much of a word is most of it, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: a piazza is an Italian town square

indicators.note: messy suggests the letters of den are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone frittering things away in an Italian square next to an untidy room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' drops the last letter of the town square; 'messy' scrambles 'den'; 'bordering' wraps the shortened square round that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander money or time is to fritter it away, synonymous with wasting it.

clue.text: Forestall old boy through note

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
via means by way of, through
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A former pupil heads off trouble by sending a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate a problem is to prevent it in advance, synonymous with forestalling it.

clue.text: Unusual pub item, barrel, not to be disturbed

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put in a strange, new arrangement

explanation.surface: An odd piece of pub furniture, a barrel, that must be left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges PUB ITEM and BARREL, thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone imperturbable stays calm whatever happens: impossible to ruffle or upset.

clue.text: Southern church perhaps involves ministry full of intrigue

indicators.note: involves means takes in or wraps around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: eg, for example, means perhaps
Min is the abbreviation for ministry

explanation.surface: A church in the south takes on a ministry and becomes a hotbed of plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' gives the abbreviation for 'for example'; 'involves' has it wrap round the ministry's short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone scheming is constantly plotting and devising crafty plans, given to intrigue.

clue.text: Prepare for action keel scratched at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's keel gets damaged out on the ocean as the crew ready for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the thirteen letters of KEEL SCRATCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval idiom: warships cleared their decks of loose gear before battle, so it means get ready for action.

clue.text: Daughter during dinner maybe will get award

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A girl at dinner is going to receive a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts D inside MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is a metal disc given as an award for achievement or bravery.

clue.text: Dubious English queen with one noisy following

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
vocal means outspoken, loud

explanation.surface: A questionable English queen with a loud entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something equivocal is ambiguous and open to doubt, hence questionable.

clue.text: Joy about origins of excellent victory — and exalted feeling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: elation is great joy

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Delight at a fine win, and a feeling of being on top of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' takes the opening letters of 'excellent victory', and 'about' has the word for joy go round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation can mean a raised, lofty state of mind or spirit, an exalted feeling.

clue.text: A period recalled in stadium

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a period of time is an era, so a period is an era

explanation.surface: A former age remembered inside a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns AN ERA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed area for sport or spectacle, much the same as a stadium.

clue.text: Interfere in Florida city broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the air, spoken, so the city name is heard

parts.note: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida

explanation.surface: Someone meddles in the radio coverage of a Florida city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TAMPA and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamper with something is to meddle with it improperly, to interfere.

clue.text: A GP's practice?

parts.note: not the surgery building but what a general practitioner practises: the profession of healing

explanation.surface: A GP's practice?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice' suggests the doctor's premises; read it instead as the discipline a doctor practises.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors practise the science of healing, so a GP's practice is the field of healing itself.

clue.text: Abandoned ride with Celt insurgent

indicators.note: insurgent means rebellious, rising up, so these letters revolt into a new order

explanation.surface: A forsaken horseman riding out with a rebellious Celt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insurgent' rearranges RIDE and CELT.
explanation.definitionFit: Derelict property is deserted and left to decay, so it is abandoned.

clue.text: Far from speeding like a bullet, possibly?

definitions.text: Far from speeding like a bullet, possibly?

parts.words: Far from speeding like a bullet, possibly?
parts.note: a slug is slang for a bullet, so slug-like might seem to mean fast, yet the garden slug is notoriously slow

explanation.surface: Something that is anything but quick, unlike a fired bullet.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: a slug is a bullet, but also the slowest of garden creatures, so 'like a bullet' playfully suggests the slow word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish means slow-moving and lethargic, the very opposite of going at speed.

clue.text: Police on island about to probe law getting mockery

indicators.note: to probe is to go into, so these pieces are placed within the other

parts.note: a rule is a law or regulation

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the police come after the island

parts.note: DI, detective inspector, stands for the police
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Officers on an island investigating a law face scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the police after the island; 'to probe' sends island, police and 'about' into the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridicule is derisive laughter or contempt, synonymous with mockery.

clue.text: Clubs with reason to struggle become rough

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: to struggle is to writhe and twist, so the letters of reason are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer with good grounds to battle grows hardened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to struggle' rearranges REASON into OARSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To coarsen is to grow crude or harsh in texture or manner, to roughen.

clue.text: Poor sort of game discontented rabble

indicators.note: sort of suggests a version of the word, so game is rearranged
discontented means with its contents removed, leaving only the outer letters of rabble

explanation.surface: An unhappy mob watches a pretty dismal match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GAME into MEAG; 'discontented' leaves RE from RABBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or inadequate in amount or quality, hence poor.

clue.text: Flexible direction keeps Liberal in charge

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A management instruction that leaves a Liberal running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts L inside EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic stretches and springs back, so it is pliable and adaptable.

clue.text: Rush in professional life

definitions.meaning: to move headlong at great speed
a person's working history and occupation

explanation.surface: Hurrying through one's working years.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to hurtle along wildly; a career is the course of someone's working life.

clue.text: A cricket club shown by artist in capital

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a stock artist

explanation.surface: A cricket club is displayed alongside a painter in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: ACCRA is the capital of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of the West African nation of Ghana.

clue.text: Undertaking to play a great timeless tune

indicators.note: to play with letters is to rearrange them
timeless means without time, and T is the abbreviation for time, so that letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A promise to perform a wonderful, classic melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops T from TUNE, leaving UNE; 'to play' rearranges A GREAT with UNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a formal promise or pledge, a binding undertaking.

clue.text: Journey close to home for meat dish

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: close means end, so the end letter of home is taken

explanation.surface: A trip near the house for a plate of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPE is the stomach lining of cattle, cooked as a dish in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is edible offal from a cow's stomach, served as a meat dish.

clue.text: Overwhelming result scored via a lot of crosses?

definitions.text: Overwhelming result scored via a lot of crosses?

parts.words: Overwhelming result scored via a lot of crosses?
parts.note: crosses are the marks voters put on ballot papers, so a huge number of them wins an election by a vast margin

explanation.surface: A football rout built on many balls crossed into the box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' suggests football passes; here they are ballot-paper marks, and the result is an election.
explanation.definitionFit: An election won by an enormous majority is a crushing, overwhelming victory.

clue.text: Packed hotel welcomes credit? On the contrary

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so one piece goes inside another
on the contrary reverses the roles, so the credit takes in the hotel rather than vice versa

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A crowded hotel accepts credit, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' with 'On the contrary' puts H inside TICK, not TICK inside H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thick is dense and closely crowded, as in a wood thick with trees: packed.

clue.text: Popular account in document proving appropriate

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a charter is a formal document

explanation.surface: A well-liked report in a document turns out to be fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' gives letters for popular; the 'in' after 'account' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is typical of someone fits their nature, so it is fitting or suitable for them.
